Users can now use the Adobe Firefly AI assistant to create fully licensed music, voiceovers, and sound effects. Here's the full rundown.

Firefly audio tools officially arrive

Adobe previously collaborated with Berklee College of Music on a survey examining the workflows and challenges faced by video creators, musicians, and marketers. Adobe said all respondents reported using music in their videos, with 32.7% using AI-generated music. 43.2% of respondents identified legal and copyright risks as the biggest obstacle to using music, while 38.9% pointed to licensing fees.

Adobe today announced that the Generate Music tool is now available on Firefly, alongside two other tools: Generate Speech and Generate Sound Effects.

Generate Music can create original, fully licensed music based on video length and mood, which users can use on any platform without worrying about licensing or takedowns. Generate Speech converts text into clear, natural-sounding voiceovers, with users able to choose between Adobe's own Firefly voice models or options from ElevenLabs. Generate Sound Effects creates custom sound effects based on on-screen action and timing.

The company emphasises that music generated by Generate Music is fully licensed and can be used directly in finished productions; like Generate Speech and Generate Sound Effects, users do not need an additional subscription to generate assets usable for commercial purposes.

Generate Music can analyse video content and automatically build editable prompts based on what it deems the most fitting style. Users can also adjust parameters such as tempo, energy, and length before hitting the "Generate" button to receive four options.

With Generate Speech, users can add emotional expression and pronunciation tags to specific parts of their scripts; Generate Sound Effects allows users to input text prompts or record audio references to generate sound effects.

The following content is provided by Adobe:

The new tools are now available on Adobe Firefly for desktop and mobile web apps.

Adobe expands AI model lineup within Firefly

Additionally, Adobe also announced today that Gemini Omni Flash is coming to Firefly, allowing users to "combine video, audio, and image inputs with text to provide more ways to develop and iterate on video…"

This move comes just days after the company added Runway Aleph 2.0 and Kling 2.0 to its third-party model toolkit, which already includes models from Google, Kling AI, Luma AI, OpenAI, Runway, and Adobe itself.
